H = (h-bar * omega / 2) * Z
Z|0> = +1|0>,   Z|1> = -1|1>

H|0> = (+h-bar*omega/2) |0>   <- energy = +h-bar*omega/2
H|1> = (-h-bar*omega/2) |1>   <- energy = -h-bar*omega/2

energy gap = h-bar * omega
caption: |0⟩ and |1⟩ are this Hamiltonian's energy eigenstates — the standard simplified model for real qubit hardware.

steps.label: U(t)|0⟩ only picks up a global phase (Lesson 26)
steps.sub: Invisible — P(0)=1, P(1)=0 forever, no matter how much time passes

steps.label: That's exactly what 'stationary state' means
steps.sub: Probabilities frozen in time, even as the phase technically rotates

steps.label: |+⟩ is NOT an energy eigenstate of this H
steps.sub: It mixes both energies, so its relative phase drifts observably

steps.label: Real qubit hardware has two distinct energy levels
steps.sub: Superconducting circuits, trapped ions, electron/nuclear spins

steps.label: The gap ħω sets a physical control frequency
steps.sub: Literally the frequency of the microwave or laser pulses used

steps.label: That frequency sets how fast gates can run
steps.sub: Real tradeoffs between gate speed, stability, and noise
